terms.definition: An atom that has gained or lost electrons, so it carries an electric charge.
terms.function: The charged particle that forms ionic bonds and conducts in solution.
terms.whereItIs: Na⁺ and Cl⁻ — the charged atoms in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Ions drive nerve signals, batteries, and the chemistry of salt.

terms.definition: A positive ion, formed when an atom loses electrons.
terms.function: The electron giver — becomes positive because it now has more protons than electrons.
terms.whereItIs: Sodium as Na⁺ in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Cations pair with anions to build ionic compounds.

terms.definition: A negative ion, formed when an atom gains electrons.
terms.function: The electron taker — becomes negative because it now has more electrons than protons.
terms.whereItIs: Chlorine as Cl⁻ in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Anions pair with cations to build ionic compounds.

terms.definition: The pull between a positive and a negative ion.
terms.function: Binds ions together into ionic compounds like table salt.
terms.whereItIs: The glow band between Na⁺ and Cl⁻ in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: This attraction is the basis of ionic bonding.
